reason: The cited evidence (E1) confirms Cr-V-rich precipitates form in the baseline alloy at 8 dpa, but neither E1 nor E2 provides any data on Hf additions, Hf segregation behavior, or Hf effects on Cr-V mobility in this alloy system; the key premises about Hf are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Hf segregates to grain boundaries in W38Ta36Cr15V11 during annealing at ~800°C
Hf at grain boundaries reduces Cr and V mobility and suppresses Cr-V-rich precipitate formation
